summary: Remove the database-wide advisory lock from events.Broker.Append (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/events/broker.go:85); each write keeps only its owner row lock, so one issue's events keep their order and different issues never wait. Every reader that pages events by a global id cursor (SSE handler and Last-Event-ID resume, event stream relay, delivery hub catch-up, GET /references?since=, and INFRA-607's planned sweep) reads only up to a safe horizon from a new events.Horizon: an observation is one statement (max(id), pg_current_snapshot(), the observer's own xid) committed with synchronous_commit off, and it is safe once a later snapshot's xmin is above that xid. Readers keep id order, so no client cursor changes.

findings.finding: F1: one snapshot's xip misses transactions with xid at or above its xmax, so 'H = A when xip is empty' can skip a row.
findings.answer: Observation adds the observer's own xid X (assigned after the snapshot); safe once a later snapshot's xmin > X. Test T3b scripts the counterexample.

findings.finding: F2: cold since = relay cursor races with a page the relay published before advancing.
findings.answer: Relay holds one mutex across publish+advance and subscribe+read; SSE uses the cursor returned with the subscription. Test T4. Agreed with INFRA-606, which implements the same rule.

findings.finding: F3: horizon valid only on the primary.
findings.answer: Primary-only constraint written in the architecture doc and sent to the architect for INFRA-63.

findings.finding: F4: a per-session advisory lock creates deadlock cycles (accept path, pending delivery, broadcasts).
findings.answer: No per-session lock. Non-conflicting transactions have no defined order; every ownerless append follows its own row lock; the implementer confirms each site and documents it in Append.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance line 1: 'a write holds no lock shared with writes to other issues'. Read literally, this includes Postgres's NOTIFY commit lock (async.c PreCommit_Notify, LockSharedObject on database 0, held through commit), which every event write takes through trigger 0107, and every document append and delivery-change write takes too.
specDepartures.plan: Removes the advisory lock and every lock held from the append to commit across issues; keeps trigger 0107 and measures waits on the NOTIFY commit lock on the load run; sends the decision (D1) to the architect, recommending its own child covering all three notifies.
specDepartures.evidence: Postgres REL_16_STABLE src/backend/commands/async.c lines 939-956; store/migrations/0107_events_notify.up.sql; docs/persistence.go:238-243 and docs/stale_room.go:27-51 (INFRA-556's lane); migration 0100; INFRA-607 and INFRA-590 plan to wake on dispatch_events.
